item.title: Red Sox Should Consider Predicted $118M Pitcher if Sonny Gray Leaves in Free Agency
item.description: Red Sox Should Consider Predicted $118M Pitcher if Sonny Gray Leaves in Free Agency originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With the possibility of losing right-hander Sonny Gray in MLB free agency, the Boston Red Sox will have to figure out who they want to replace him with. The reality is that there aren’t many great starting pitchers available in Major League Baseball this offseason, and teams like the Red Sox will have to consider that. However, one player makes a ton of sense for Boston: right-hander Michael King. King is a Northeast guy, went to school at Northeastern, and has played for the New York Yankees throughout his career. All of those factors make him a perfect candidate to join a team like the Red Sox, though his contract situation does lead to some questions. King is expected to land a deal worth over $100 million, with the latest prediction recently suggesting that he could be a four-year, $118 million man. However, it was also noted that he really enjoys his time with the San Diego Padres. “I expect King to opt out of the two remaining player-option years on his contract so he can receive a $5 million buyout and then look to secure a long-term contract. King had a terrific year with the Padres, posting a 3.21 ERA in 185 innings over 32 starts. He’s from the East Coast but has really enjoyed his time with the Padres, considers San Diego his second home and has sincere interest in staying. San Diego desperately needs to re-sign him, as he’s clearly the ace of their staff,” Jim Bowden said . With King now a free agent, baseball expects he'll at least listen to other teams around the league. He's coming off a ridiculous postseason, showing that he has the stuff to be among the best in baseball at any given moment. He was perhaps better than anybody in the playoffs this year, appearing in three games, starting two of them, and posting a 0.64 ERA in 14.0 innings. More Red Sox Latest Red Sox news Fenway Park fan guide: What to know before you go Complete history of Red Sox championships

item.title: Boxing pound-for-pound rankings (Nov. 2026): Canelo Alvarez storms back into top 10 after Mbilli masterclass
item.description: Saul "Canelo" Alvarez is back among boxing's pound-for-pound best. More than a year after Terence Crawford stripped him of his undisputed crown, Alvarez reminded the boxing world that he remains one of its elite fighters with a dominant decision victory over Christian Mbilli this past Saturday in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The victory not only returned a world title to Alvarez's waist , but also proved that, even at the tail end of his career, the Mexican superstar remains a step above the rest of the super middleweight division . On the women’s side, with Katie Taylor's final dance behind us , there is a consensus No. 1 fighter for the first time since Uncrowned began its women’s pound-for-pound rankings in December 2024. November's list also welcomed a debut entrant on the men's side and a return for one of women’s boxing’s elite names. Uncrowned's panel of experts — Kel Dansby, Alan Dawson, Darshan Desai, Joseph Santoliquito, Lewis Watson and Elliot Worsell — have ranked the men's and women's pound-for-pound best, one through 10, using a weighted points system to determine the final rankings. (Being voted No. 1 equals 10 points, No. 2 equals nine points, down to No. 10 equaling one point.) Without further ado, here are our pound-for-pound rankings for November 2026! MEN'S POUND-FOR-POUND RANKINGS The undisputed king of the ring. (Photo by Yuichi YAMAZAKI / AFP via Getty Images) YUICHI YAMAZAKI via Getty Images 1. Naoya Inoue — Undisputed super bantamweight champion (Prev: 1) News about Naoya Inoue's next move is imminent. After scoring the finest win of his career in May when he outclassed Junto Nakatani in the biggest boxing match in Japan’s history , Inoue is now targeting another battle of top pound-for-pound fighters with Jesse "Bam" Rodriguez. The pair are in talks for a March superfight in Japan. If that doesn't materialize, Inoue will look to challenge for a world title at featherweight and become just the seventh fighter in men's boxing history to be able to call himself a five-division champion. Whichever is next for Inoue, he’s proving he is still very much a legacy fighter even in the years past his prime. 2T. Oleksandr Usyk — Former undisputed cruiserweight and heavyweight champion (Prev: 2) Oleksandr Usyk is another name who isn’t done adding to his legacy just yet. After winning Olympic gold and undisputed titles at both cruiserweight and heavyweight, it seemed that Usyk, 39, was no longer interested in facing the top contenders and consistently proving himself to be the No. 1 fighter on the planet. Usyk took a novelty fight with Rico Verhoeven in May , and then elected to drop his belts rather than defend them against Agit Kabayel. The Ukrainian appeared to be angling for a past-his-best version of Deontay Wilder for one of the final fights of his career — and who could blame him? item.title: 76ers coach Nick Nurse provides update on Joel Embiid’s right plantar fascia injury management
item.description: Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images 76ers coach Nick Nurse provides update on Joel Embiid’s right plantar fascia injury management appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Coach Nick Nurse ’s Philadelphia 76ers were 6-1 on the season heading into November 2’s home game against the Chicago Bulls and riding high in the latest NBA Power Rankings . Star center Joel Embiid found himself on the injury report as fans wondered if he’d play or not. Nurse addressed Embiid’s right plantar fasciitis injury in comments shared by Dave Uram of SPORTSRADIO 94WIP. “Plantar’s a little bit of a come-and-go type of thing, so they’re just trying to manage it, it’s very painful, it can kinda come-and-go outta nowhere, so just trying to manage the pain of that,” Nurse said when asked if there is a concern about the situation. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Embiid has missed two games this season and has averaged 35.2 minutes in the games he has played, averaging 19.2 points per game but shooting an uncharacteristically low 40 percent from the field. He ranks third on Nurse’s team in scoring behind Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown, and slightly ahead of LeBron James, who is scoring nearly three points less per game. The Sixers have found an intriguing level of balance and effectiveness on offense even with Embiid ailing. Plantar fasciitis is the type of injury that can last for months on end, which will put pressure on Embiid to learn how to play at a slower pace at times. Nurse, for his part, is embracing the bumps in the road that come with the frustrating injury, while leaning on Brown and Maxey to carry the scoring load. The Sixers have outrageously good depth heading toward the end of the calendar year, meaning they can afford to keep Embiid out for the time being if they deem more rest to be necessary. Related: ClutchPoints’ 2026-27 NBA Power Rankings Week 3: Rockets, Pistons, 76ers take top spots amid league-wide injury concerns Related: Early Paul George vs. Jaylen Brown comparison shows Celtics getting better of 76ers trade

item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon State’s loss at Fresno State
item.description: FRESNO, Calif. — Oregon State lost to Fresno State 38-22 Saturday night at Valley Children’s Stadium. Here are 10 takeaways as the Beavers prepare to host Texas State. 1. Reality check Two things can be true. Oregon State can still be ahead of schedule and on its way to a legitimately surprising season amid a massive rebuild, complete with a potent offense. Much of its success thus far came by pounding less talented teams and several of the worst defenses in the country. And where OSU was vulnerable was there to be exploited by teams like Fresno State, which has talent and good coaching. The Beavers are not a College Football Playoff team. That dose of reality doesn’t diminish what’s being accomplished this season. They’re simply not one of the two most talented teams in the Pac-12 right now. 2. Oregon State was outcoached JaMarcus Shephard and his staff were outcoached for definitely the first time in conference play and arguably for the first time this season. Matt Entz laid out in detail what Fresno State picked up from studying Braden Atkinson from his time at Mercer and Oregon State’s tendencies. Bye weeks also include self-scouting. Fresno State was more prepared for what OSU showed and particularly offensively the Beavers did not have an effective counter. 3. Self-inflicted errors can’t happen in games like this Winning on the road against a team with at least comparable (if not better) talent and coaching is a difficult task to begin with. It becomes a whole lot harder with six presnap penalties and allowing five sacks with two leading to fumbles. OSU absolutely could have led by multiple scores early if not for a false start negating Jake Reichle’s would-be touchdown, if Aeryn Hampton’s foot was in bounds and if multiple other penalties didn’t occur. That doesn’t even get into defensive miscues from missed tackles or over-pursuits. 4. The offensive line may have had its worst game Houston was more physically dominating than Fresno State, but that’s to be expected. Oregon State’s offensive line had a brutal showing nearly across the board, with sacks allowed by multiple players in one-on-one matchups. OSU’s rushing stats are skewed by the sacks and not nearly as poor as the final box score, but the bottom line is Fresno State won the line of scrimmage and it’s not a particularly stout group. 5. Josiah Freeman was the best receiver on the field Fresno State’s 6-foot-4 receiver had a big night with two touchdowns. Freeman had a massive advantage against Isaiah Houi and performed accordingly. If there’s one piece OSU’s receiving corps is missing it is a target with the size and length of Freeman, which the Beavers are leaning on via their tight ends. But an outside target like him is hard to beat and he showed why. 6. Tackling, leverage issues persist OSU showed a vulnerability early, but against Houston and Texas Tech it was understandable in terms of talent and timing on the schedule. item.title: Houston Rockets jersey history No. 40 - Dick Gibbs (1971-72)
item.description: The Houston Rockets have had players donning a total of 52 different jersey numbers (and have one not part of any numerical series for Houston assistant coach and general manager Carroll Dawson) since their founding at the start of the 1967-68 season, worn by just under 500 players in the course of Rockets history. To honor all of the players who wore those numbers over the decades, Rockets Wire is covering the entire history of jersey numbers and the players who wore them since the founding of the team all those years ago right up to the present day. With seven of those jerseys now retired to honor some of the greatest Rockets of all time to wear those jerseys, there is a lot of history to cover. And for today's article, we will continue with the first of eight who wore the No. 40, Dick Gibbs. After ending his college career at Texas-El Paso, Gibbs was picked up with the 49th overall selection of the 1971 NBA Draft by the Chicago Bulls. The Ames, Iowa native played the first 2 seasons of his pro career with the Houston Rockets instead, coming to an end when he had his contract sold to the (then) Kansas City-Omaha (now, Sacramento) Kings in 1972. During his time suiting up for the Rockets, Gibbs wore only jersey No. 40 and put up 3.7 points and 2.2 rebounds per game. All stats and data courtesy of Basketball Reference. This article originally appeared on Rockets Wire: Houston Rockets jersey history No. 40 - Dick Gibbs (1971-72)

item.title: Every player from California to play for the Brooklyn Nets - Darwin Cook
item.description: The Brooklyn Nets have signed, drafted, and traded for players from virtually every state in the US, and much of the wider world beyond the United States. From Alabama to Wyoming, and from Australia to Ukraine, the Nets have a long and distinguished history of turning over every stone to find the talent needed to succeed in the NBA. From their start in the American Basketball Association (ABA) as the New Jersey Americans and New York Nets to their jump to the NBA as the New Jersey Nets right through to today, the organization has cast their net for talent wide since the inception of the ball club. For this installment of our series documenting the provenience of every Nets player to suit up for the franchise, let's take a look at every player from California who has played for Brooklyn. Our focus in this article is Darwin Cook. An alum of University of Portland, he was picked up with the 70th overall selection of the 1980 NBA Draft by the Detroit Pistons . The Los Angeles, California native played the first 6 seasons of his pro career with the (then) New Jersey (now, Brooklyn) Nets instead, coming to an end when he was dealt to the (then) Washington Bullets (now, Wizards) in 1986. During his time suiting up for the Nets, Darwin Cook put up 10.1 points, 2.3 rebounds, 4.2 assists, and 1.9 steals per game. All stats and data courtesy of Basketball Reference. This article originally appeared on Nets Wire: Every player from California to play for the Brooklyn Nets - Darwin Cook

item.title: Every player from California to play for the Golden State Warriors - Lou Amundson
item.description: The Golden State Warriors have signed, drafted, and traded for players from nearly every U.S. state and many countries around the world. From Alaska to Wyoming and Austria to Zaire, the Warriors have a strong history of seeking out talent necessary for NBA success. Since their beginnings in the Basketball Association of America (a precursor to the NBA) when they got their start as the team representing Philadelphia before they made their move to the West Coast, the organization has consistently pursued talent from a broad range of sources. For this installment of our series taking stock of the birthplace of every Golden State player to suit up for the franchise, let's take a look at every player from California who has played for the Warriors. Our focus in this article is Lou Amundson. An alum of UNLV, he went unselected in the 2006 NBA Draft, playing in other leagues until he signed with the Utah Jazz in 2007. The Ventura, California native played the first season of his pro career with the Jazz. He also played for the Philadelphia 76ers and Phoenix Suns before he signed with the Golden State Warriors in 2010. His stay with the team lasted until he was dealt to the Indiana Pacers in 2011. During his time suiting up for the Warriors, Amundson put up 4.3 points and 4.0 rebounds per game. All stats and data courtesy of Basketball Reference. This article originally appeared on Warriors Wire: Every player from California to play for the Golden State Warriors - Lou Amundson

item.title: Matt Barrie: Final month of CFB season will be ‘tipping point’ that dictates ‘next 10 years’
item.description: Credit: The Matt Barrie Show Many college football commentators have already declared the 2026 season among the best of all time, and it could cement itself as such this weekend if Notre Dame-Miami, BYU-Utah, Alabama-LSU, and several other games live up to expectations. After that, rivalry week and conference championship season will only add to the fireworks heading into the College Football Playoff. It’s enough for ESPN’s Matt Barrie to declare the final month of the college football season a “tipping point” for the sport that will shift how it is run and covered for the next decade or more. “We have four weekends left in the regular season … the schedule-makers did their job because they’re giving us an all-time weekend in the first weekend of November,” he said Sunday on his podcast , The Matt Barrie Show. “And then little by little, this last four weeks of the regular season, the ball that we’re about to see is going to be one of those months … that we look back on at the end of the season and next year and the year after, we’re going to look at this as a tipping point in college football. “Because we’ve been saying it all year, parity, NIL has flattened out rosters. And now we’re at the new norm, and how this thing plays out over the next four years could dictate how we approach this sport for the next 10 years. Because if Wake Forest goes on another run and pulls an Indiana, what are we doing with these Blue Bloods? I’m trying to find schools that historically have nothing, and because of the way college football is now, have everything.” This week the CFP committee will also announce its first weekly rankings during a primetime broadcast on ESPN. Barrie pleaded with the committee to do the hard work of evaluating teams’ performance rather than resorting to standings and head-to-head results. “Now we get to the point where we think, based on the matchups, it’ll be settled on the field,” he said. “And I say we think that because every time you think it matters on the field, the committee will come out and do something to completely throw that away. I just hope, I really hope — because we’re going to 24 — and I hope that within this 12, they dig in and they watch and they look and they see. Because you’ve gotta get this right. Because we’ve been handed the greatest season of all time, and the last thing we need is a room of committee members to screw it up.” A season defined by upsets and chaos still needs a champion. And college football is such that the champion will, in part, be chosen subjectively. Barrie’s larger point that the results of this season will change the sport is worth considering. Even if a Cinderella like Wake Forest doesn’t shock the world, NCAA and conference leadership has to be taking note of the parity among schools and conferences, and especially the value of the regular season as an entertainment product and a way to determine excellence. item.title: How Novak Djokovic, Rafael Nadal and Roger Federer performed in their first events as world number one
item.description: Alexander Zverev became the 30th official world number one on Monday. Zverev snatched the top spot from Jannik Sinner after defeating Tallon Griekspoor in the Vienna Open round of 16 last week. Zverev is now set to compete in the Paris Masters – his first tournament as world number one. With Zverev assuming the top spot, let’s take a look back at how some of tennis’ greatest players performed upon achieving world number one status. Novak Djokovic won the Canadian Open Djokovic claimed the world number one ranking from Rafael Nadal after defeating Frenchman Jo-Wilfried Tsonga in the 2011 Wimbledon semi-finals. “They don’t give you a lot of chances to become number one,” Djokovic said afterwards with a smile. “I guess you need to lose only one match in seven months to get there.” The Serb went on to win his first title at the All England Club, beating Nadal in the final. Djokovic carried his excellent form to Montreal, defeating Nikolay Davydenko, Marin Cilic, Gael Monfils, Jo-Wilfried Tsonga and Mardy Fish en route to the title. In securing the title, Djokovic became the first player to win five Masters 1000 events [since the format alteration in 2009]. “History-making, of course it’s special,” Djokovic said after beating Fish in the final. “Of course, it’s an honour and privilege to be part of the history of the sport that I love and that I play.” Rafael Nadal lost to Andy Murray at the US Open Nadal achieved the world number one ranking after winning gold at the 2008 Olympic Games in Beijing. The Spaniard, who defeated Chile’s Fernando Gonzalez in the gold-medal match, overtook Roger Federer to claim the top spot. “That year [2008], Novak started to play so well. For me it was another tough rival, so I thought, well, I have been there [at the top level], but I didn’t achieve the world number one. Now another great player is coming, so maybe I will never be No. 1,” Nadal told the ATP in 2025. Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images “So for me that’s why it was so important for me to achieve that. I believe that I deserved it after having a very high level almost in every week during three and a half years.” After assuming the number one ranking, Nadal competed in the US Open. The Spaniard defeated Sam Querrey and Mardy Fish en route to the semi-finals, before losing to Andy Murray in four sets. Roger Federer helped Swiss win their Davis Cup tie Federer debuted as world number one after defeating Juan Carlos Ferrero in the 2004 Australian Open semi-finals. Federer went on to win the title in Melbourne, beating Marat Safin in the final. “I’m happy to have had a great start now to the season, and to finally be number one,” Federer said at the time. “And it does make me feel really strange.” Photo by GREG WOOD/AFP via Getty Images The Swiss star then represented his nation in their Davis Cup match against Romania. item.title: How USC’s JuJu Watkins performed in 1st game back in 588 days vs. UNLV
item.description: Robert Hanashiro-USA TODAY Sports How USC’s JuJu Watkins performed in 1st game back in 588 days vs. UNLV appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jujuj Watkins is back on the court for USC Women’s Basketball. Watkins returned ot the court for USC against UNLV on Monday after missing over a year recovering from a torn ACL. Watkins first game back was nothing short of phenomenal . Watkins scored 21 points, with five rebounds, two assists, and two steals in 24 minutes, starting strong in her first game in 588 days. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Watkins broke out in 2023-24 as a freshman, leading USC to the Elite Eight against UConn. She played in 34 games that year, averaging 27.1 points per game with 7.3 rebounds, 3.3 assists, 2.3 steals, and 1.6 blocks per game. The next season, she led the Trojans to the fourth overall seed and the number one seed in the Spokane Regional. For a second straight season, USC fell in the Elite Eight to UConn, but that game was without Watkins on the court. She had put together another stellar season, scoring 23.9 points, with 6.8 rebounds, 3.4 assists, 2.2 steals and 1.8 blocks per game. She dominated in the first round of the NCAA Tournament, putting up 22 points and eight rebounds. The next game was against Mississippi State. She played just five minutes, scoring three points with a rebound and an assist before going down with an injury. Without Watkins in the lineup, USC was not able to make the same run in the NCAA Tournament as they did the previous year. USC lost in the second round of the Big Ten tournament. They would then win their first-round game against Clemson as a nine seed, but fall to South Carolina in the second round. The Trojans are 1-0 on the season after their 100-68 win over UNLV. They return to the court on Sunday to face off against Utah State. item.title: The Cadillac F1 Team is For Sale – If You Have $3 Billion
item.description: Rumors have been swirling for months and now it appears, where there's smoke, there's fire. And we're not just talking about the Cadillac F1 team's brake issues. Mark Walter is reportedly exploring a sale of his Cadillac Formula 1 stake, with an asking price of no less than $3 billion and at least seven interested parties, according to three people familiar with the process. The team is wrapping up its debut F1 season, and despite an even worse than anticipated campaign, that doesn't seem to have had any impact on the valuation. Walter controls the team through TWG Global, which houses his racing holdings in F1, IndyCar, and NASCAR under its TWG Motorsports division. The operation is run jointly with General Motors and its Cadillac subsidiary. TWG holds controlling ownership, although the split between the partners has not been disclosed. The firm had not responded to inquiries about the sale. The move would reverse a position TWG stated plainly just last month. Once Walter agreed to sell the Los Angeles Lakers to Joshua Kushner and Bob Iger for $12.5 billion, the firm ruled out any sale of the Cadillac F1 team or MLB's Los Angeles Dodgers. "TWG is not considering exiting its stake in the Cadillac Formula 1 team or any other part of TWG Motorsports," the firm said in a long statement. That statement addressed speculation about Walter's sports portfolio after he drew scrutiny over undisclosed related-party dealings at insurance companies he controls through Guggenheim Partners, the firm he co-founded and leads as CEO. The nondisclosures spurred two federal investigations. Walter has also sold his 13% stake in Chelsea to Clearlake Capital, and he is reportedly seeking a buyer for the WNBA's Los Angeles Sparks at $700 million. On the Dodgers, Walter said last week, "We are going to keep the team no matter what." To launch the operation, the partners paid a $450 million dilution fee and committed at least $1 billion more. The team is reportedly tracking toward a loss of about $400 million this year, a figure driven largely by startup costs and a commercial business that is still building. On track, Cadillac has yet to score a point, and Sergio Perez extended his contract through at least 2029 last week. F1 valuations have climbed sharply with the cost cap and Liberty Media's commercial expansion. Sportico valued the 10 grid teams at an average of $3.42 billion last year, up 48% and more than double its 2023 average of $1.61 billion.

item.title: Ex-Lions LB reflects on life-altering injury after Jack Campbell hospitalized
item.description: Reggie Brown, the former linebacker for the Detroit Lions , said he will visit a psychologist at 12:15 p.m. Tuesday near his home in Houston, as he has every other week for the last 15 years He said he used to wonder why he was angry before he started therapy. Then he learned he was clinically depressed. Then he began taking medication, developing more coping mechanicsms and exploring the effects of a spinal-cord injury that Brown suffered during a Lions game in 1997. CPR saved his life. But the injury altered it ... and ended his football career at 23. “I used to be Superman, but now I wear Kryptonite all around,’’ Brown told USA TODAY Sports. “You know, it's a struggle getting out of the bed, but once I get going and make it to the shower … “I had my days where I can go to some dark corners in my mind. But I have a wife, kids, some real positive things. Kind of just got to go through those emotions and still seek out those things I'm grateful for.” Brown, 52, reflected on his experience during an interview with USA TODAY Sports Monday, Nov. 2, after learning Lions linebacker Jack Campbell suffered a neck injury that left him hospitalized . “I'll be praying for him,’’ Brown said. Lions head coach Dan Campbell on Monday told reporters he could provide no specifics about Jack Campbell’s condition . But he did say “it’s positive’’ and “it’s a small setback.’’ But for Brown, the injury has led to almost three decades of recovery and struggle. He said that includes two neck surgeries. "So now I'm up to a total of six screws a titanium plate in my neck,'' he said. JACK CAMPBELL INJURY UPDATE: Lions share 'positive news' on LB after neck injury 'Maybe I'll go next year' Brown said he wasn’t watching the Lions game during Jack Campbell’s injury on the first play of the fourth quarter. “I couldn't tell you the last time I watched the entire game,’’ he said. “But, you know, I'll leave it on for a little while.’’ The last time Brown attended a Lions game was 2007, when his brother Michael was a safety for the New York Giants during a game against the Lions. He also said he was invited back last season before a ‘’homecoming game,’’ when the New York Jets played the Lions Sept. 28, 2026. “And I've been wanting to go,’’ Brown said. “Somebody reached out to me, said I kind of need to go.’’ But Brown said he and Jets head coach Aaron Glenn played together at Texas A&M, and that Glenn was on the field when Brown suffered the spinal-cord injury in 1997. And it turned out the Jets-Lions game was on Brown’s birthday. He stayed in Houston rather than go to the game. “Yeah, too many coincidences,’’ Brown said. “…Maybe I'll go next year.’’ But Brown expresses no bitterness toward football and never tried to hold his two sons back. His oldest son, Reggie Brown Jr. played tight end at Tulane from 2020 to 2024. His youngest son, Mike, is a freshman wide receiver at Texas A&M. item.title: YPP’s Agada wants end to raw material exports
item.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — The presidential candidate of the Young Progressives Party (YPP), Arch. Peter Agada, has called for an end to the export of Nigeria’s raw materials without adding value, saying the practice deprives the country of greater economic benefits. Agada spoke in an interview in Abuja on Monday while outlining his economic blueprint ahead of the 2027 general elections. He said his proposed administration would prioritise electricity supply and promote industrialisation from the ward level to ensure that value was added to Nigerian produce before export. “The industrialisation we all talk about can only happen when we fix power and put in place policies that will promote investments from the ward level upwards,” Agada said. He said rural communities would be made attractive to agro-allied industries capable of processing agricultural produce for export and generating foreign exchange. “Our rural communities will attract agro-allied industries to promote export of produce after value has been added to earn foreign exchange. Enough of sending raw materials only to collect peanuts in return,” he said. The YPP candidate also said his proposed administration would mobilise Nigerians at home and in the diaspora to build a country citizens would be proud to call home. He said this would involve building on the country’s strengths while addressing areas of weakness. On politics, Agada urged members of the political elite, irrespective of party affiliation, to allow Nigerians to freely choose their leaders at all levels. He said the practice of imposing leaders on the electorate on the basis of ethnic or religious considerations should become a thing of the past. item.title: Customs appoints Mamman Ali acting Adamawa/Taraba Comptroller
item.description: By Umar Yusuf, Yola The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has appointed Deputy Comptroller Mamman Ali as the Acting Area Comptroller of its Adamawa/Taraba Command. Ali, who was until his appointment the Coordinator of the Customs Anti-Smuggling Unit, Operation Whirlwind, Zone E, takes over from Mohammed Tako, who has been promoted to Assistant Comptroller-General of Customs in charge of Zone B, Kaduna. At a brief handing-over ceremony in Yola on Monday, Tako said the command recorded significant achievements during his tenure despite directives on strict border closure. He said the command strengthened security along critical border corridors through enhanced joint operations and patrols with sister security agencies. Tako disclosed that the total Duty Paid Value (DPV) of seizures recorded by the command during his one-year tenure stood at ₦535,975,190. He commended officers and men of the command for their cooperation during his tenure and urged them to extend the same support to his successor. In his remarks, the new Acting Area Comptroller, Ali, pledged to build on the achievements of his predecessor. He solicited the support and cooperation of sister security agencies, officers and men of the command to strengthen border policing and curb smuggling activities across Adamawa and Taraba states. item.title: Brian Sabean Humbled by Hall Of Fame Bid
item.description: Oct 31, 2014; San Francisco, CA, USA; San Francisco Giants general manager Brian Sabean speaks to the crowd during the World Series celebration at City Hall. The San Francisco Giants defeated the Kansas City Royals in game seven of the World Series. Mandatory Credit: Ed Szczepanski-USA TODAY Sports Former Giants general manager Brian Sabean knows he is not the biggest name on his Hall of Fame ballot. He told reporters on Monday that he is the only person on the list who is not a true icon in the sport. This honesty stands out in a game full of loud voices and big egos. Sabean built three championship teams in San Francisco, yet he still feels like the underdog among his peers. The New York Post reports that Sabean joined the Class of 2027 Contemporary Baseball Era ballot . He was one of eight people selected for this special group. The committee is scheduled to gather in San Diego on Dec. 6 to cast their votes. A candidate must obtain 75 percent support from the 16-person panel to gain entry. Sabean knows the odds are steep, but he remains grateful for the chance. A Rare Moment of Truth Sabean did not try to spin his story . He called the nomination “flattering” because of the strength of the ballot. He said the group is “such an august group.” His reaction was simple and direct. He told the press by phone, “I’m blown away. I’m beyond humbled.” That line cuts through the usual noise of baseball politics. Most executives would claim they deserve the spot. Sabean admitted he is lucky just to be in the room. He shares the ballot with legends like Dusty Baker and Bruce Bochy. Sabean himself hired both men to manage the Giants. The list also includes Sandy Alderson, Joe Maddon, Lou Piniella, Ted Turner, and Bill White. These names carry huge weight in the history of the game. Sabean knows he is the odd one out when it comes to fame. He told the Post, “It’s flattering because of the strength of the ballot. It’s such an august group. I think I’m the only person on it that’s not an icon in the sport.” The Yankees Connection and A New Chapter Sabean’s path to this moment is long and winding. He spent four seasons as an executive assistant to Yankees GM Brian Cashman. The organization chose not to retain him for the 2027 season. This move ended his second tenure with the team. He first worked for the Yankees in the 1980s and 1990s. He played a major role in developing the Core Four during that time. Before the Yankees, he helped draft and sign Derek Jeter, Andy Pettitte, and Mariano Rivera. These players formed the backbone of a dynasty. He later served as the GM for three championship Giants teams. His resume is full of wins. Yet, he is still fighting for recognition from the voters. The committee will look at his work from the late 20th century and beyond. They need to decide if his impact was enough to earn his place in Cooperstown. Why Humility Wins in the End Sabean’s approach is a breath of fresh air. He does not demand respect. He earns it by admitt

item.title: Shane Wright Clearly Wanted Out Of Seattle
item.description: Shane Wright may not be willing to say he asked the Seattle Kraken for a trade, but his first comments as a member of the Nashville Predators suggest he was ready for a change. The 22-year-old forward met with reporters Monday after Seattle dealt him to Nashville in exchange for Matthew Wood. When asked whether he and his representatives had requested a move, Wright gave an answer that left a little room for interpretation. “I wouldn’t say, like, we requested a trade,” Wright said speaking to Predators beat reporter Alex Daugherty. “I think for me, I just always wanted a little more opportunity, I wanted to have more minutes, wanted to play a bigger role. Whether that was in Seattle or somewhere else, I was happy to do that. But now (I’m) moving on from that situation, and I’m happy to be here.” There's a distinction worth pointing out. Wright didn't come out and say he demanded a trade, nor did he flat-out deny that a request was made. What he did acknowledge was that his situation in Seattle wasn't giving him the opportunity he wanted. Whether that meant a bigger role with the Kraken or a fresh start somewhere else, he was ready for something different. And it's not as if the possibility of Wright leaving Seattle came out of nowhere. Back in July, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that Wright's agent, Kurt Overhardt, had indicated the two sides had reached an understanding about finding the young forward a new home. Overhardt specifically said Kraken general manager Jason Botterill had agreed to move Wright during the offseason, with the goal of finding him a team in need of a young center. “I can confirm that we have had positive conversations with GM Jason Botterill, and he has agreed to move Shane this summer to a team in need of a top young center,” Overhardt said at the time, per Friedman. Botterill declined to comment on the situation when asked by Friedman. The trade eventually came Sunday, with Seattle and Nashville swapping two former first-round picks in a one-for-one deal. Wright heads to the Predators, while Wood gets a fresh opportunity with the Kraken. For Wright, the move comes after a difficult stretch in Seattle. Once projected to go No. 1 overall in the 2022 NHL Draft, he fell to the Kraken at No. 4. He made his NHL debut as an 18-year-old in 2022, but never quite developed into the top-line centerpiece Seattle had hoped he could become. He finished the 2025-26 season with 27 points (including 12 goals and 15 assists) in 74 games, down considerably from the 44 points he recorded in 79 appearances the previous season. He also had four points, including three goals, through 14 games this season before the trade. Wood, meanwhile, arrives in Seattle with a different profile. The 6-foot-4 forward was selected 15th overall by Nashville in 2023 after playing college hockey at Minnesota and UConn. item.description: Jamie LeBlanc-Imagn Images. Blue Jays decline Myles Straw’s 2027 option appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Toronto Blue Jays declined their 2027 club option on outfielder Myles Straw on Monday, sending the veteran into free agency after two seasons with the team. The option would have paid Straw $8 million next season. Instead, he receives a $1.75 million buyout, which the Cleveland Guardians cover under the terms of the trade that brought him to the Blue Jays. Straw , 32, hit .241 with a .304 on-base percentage and .342 slugging percentage in 2026. He finished with three home runs, 26 RBI and seven stolen bases across 330 plate appearances. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) MLB Network insider Jon Morosi posted the update Monday on X, formerly Twitter, confirming the Blue Jays’ decision to decline Straw’s option for the 2027 season. “Blue Jays have declined their 2027 option on Myles Straw.” Those numbers represented a step back from his first season with the Blue Jays, when he batted .262/.313/.367 with four home runs and 12 steals in 299 plate appearances. His OPS fell from .680 to .646. Toronto acquired Straw from the Guardians on January 17, 2025, receiving cash and international signing bonus pool space in the deal. He subsequently spent two seasons providing the Blue Jays with an experienced option in center field. Straw won an American League Gold Glove in 2022, establishing defense as a central part of his value. His offensive production, however, left the Blue Jays weighing whether to commit $8 million to an outfielder with limited power. He showed improvement at the plate late in the season. Beginning August 3, Straw hit .277/.348/.387 over 134 plate appearances, delivering a stronger finish than his full-season numbers suggest. That stretch could help his case as he searches for his next opportunity. The Blue Jays could still re-sign Straw at a lower salary, but he can now explore other opportunities for 2027. item.title: Adam Schefter Reveals Raiders’ Trade Plans at Deadline
item.description: Maxx Crosby with Kirk Cousins. Getty The Las Vegas Raiders were reeling amid a four-game losing streak and a winless October. This led to speculation that they would decide to be sellers at the trade deadline. The Raiders were able to get back into the win column against the New York Jets in Week 8, which complicates things. At 4-4, they are one game out of a Wild Card playoff berth. Starting to sell off assets now would send a weird message to the veterans on the team. Quarterback Kirk Cousins has been playing very well, so there should be teams interested in him. The same goes for defensive end Maxx Crosby. However, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the Raiders have no plans to trade away their top players. “The Raiders are .500 in November for the first time since 2020, I believe it is. They’re not looking to trade their players. They feel like they’re building something. They’re winning. They like this. They’re not looking to get rid of these guys,” Schefter said on the “Pat McAfee Show.” “Kirk Cousins is leading the NFL in touchdown passes. They’re not going to trade that guy. He’s a great example for Fernando Mendoza. They want to keep riding him until they fall out of playoff contention. They want to try to make the playoffs. No, Kirk Cousins, I don’t see as an option.” "The Raiders aren't looking to trade their players.. They like their team and they feel like they're building something" ~ @AdamSchefter #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/DZLmNFPI0N — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) November 2, 2026 Should Raiders Trade Away Players? It’s easy to understand both sides of the trade argument for the Raiders. Even if the team makes the playoffs, they clearly don’t have the pieces to contend for a Super Bowl. If a team like the Minnesota Vikings or Baltimore Ravens offers up a second-round pick for Cousins, it should at least be a conversation. He’s not likely to be on the team next year, and the Raiders already have the quarterback of the future on the roster. At the same time, a playoff run would be great for culture building. The Raiders should really consider any massive offers, but they don’t need to be selling key players at a discount. Cousins Turning Back the Clock The last few seasons have been tough for Cousins. He’s dealt with injuries and losing his starting job. It looked like he didn’t have much left in the tank. So far, he’s leading the NFL with 19 touchdown passes and could find himself in the MVP mix if the Raiders can start beating a couple of good teams and get into the playoffs. Head coach Klint Kubiak praised the quarterback after another strong performance against the Jets. “That’s who he’s been all year,” Kubiak said . “He’s been a leader. He’s been a playmaker for us. And that’s been the story of his season. item.title: Ogun 2027: Adebutu dismisses INEC list omission
item.description: ….Receives over 1,000 APC defectors into PDP By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta ABEOKUTA — The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, has described the omission of his name from the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) list of governorship candidates as a temporary distraction, insisting that it would not stop him from contesting the 2027 election. Adebutu spoke on Monday while receiving more than 1,000 defectors from the All Progressives Congress (APC) into the PDP at the party’s state secretariat in Abeokuta. The defectors were led by a former member of the House of Representatives, Hon. Segun William, and received by Adebutu alongside other party leaders, including the PDP’s Ogun Central senatorial candidate, Iyabo Obasanjo. Addressing the gathering, Adebutu expressed confidence that the controversy surrounding his omission from INEC’s list would be resolved, maintaining that he remained a bona fide member of the PDP. He cited his participation in elections under the party’s platform over the past two decades as evidence of his loyalty and challenged those questioning his membership to provide evidence that he had defected. “I have been the candidate of the PDP for the last 20 years, in every election cycle. My question is: at what stage did I leave or vacate the party? Where is the proof that, for one day, I have even visited the APC office, let alone joined the party?” he asked. Adebutu also said he played an active role in organising and financing the party’s recent membership registration exercise in Ogun, which he claimed recorded more than 19,800 members. He said his registration number in the exercise was 1536, describing it as further evidence of his continued membership of the party. The PDP chieftain alleged that the controversy over his omission from the INEC list was intended to distract the opposition and disenfranchise voters. He, however, urged party members to remain focused, saying the development would not disrupt the PDP’s mobilisation activities across the state. Adebutu disclosed that the party’s campaign team had visited 12 of the state’s 20 local government areas and more than 140 of its 236 wards. He said the grassroots mobilisation exercise would continue despite what he described as attempts to distract the party. “We have visited 12 of the 20 local governments. Of the 236 wards, we have visited over 140. Tomorrow, we continue again because we know that the trick is to get us distracted. We will not be distracted. We will keep our eyes on the ball, and we shall win,” he said. Earlier, William said the defectors decided to leave the APC because of their dissatisfaction with the party’s approach to governance and what he described as its failure to uphold democratic principles and deliver development in Ogun State. item.title: Inca children were drugged before being sacrificed
item.description: Figurines found alongside child mummies at Llullaillaco, on the Argentina-Chile border, and Ampato, Peru J. Reinhard Young children selected to be sacrificed as part of elaborate Inca rituals were given psychedelic and intoxicating substances, possibly to relieve the terror of their imminent death or in the belief that the drugs would help them communicate with the gods. “We cannot reconstruct the children’s emotions or determine precisely how they experienced these events,” says Dagmara Socha at the University of Warsaw, Poland. “However, we should not assume that being selected for a prestigious religious ceremony necessarily meant that the experience was not frightening or traumatic.” Read more Surprising skeletons prompt a radical rethink of Egyptian pyramids The Inca kingdom dominated 4000 kilometres of the west coast of South America from the late 13th century until the Spanish conquest of the 16th century. Advertisement In a ritual known as capacocha, children and young women were sacrificed to the mountain gods. According to an account by Spanish friar Martín de Murúa, written in 1590 , the capacocha ceremony was conducted to ensure there would be “no famine nor lack of fruits of the earth, nor would there be drought, nor pestilence, nor rebellion”. Socha and her colleagues studied eight frozen, mummified children, seven of whom were girls, discovered between the 1920s and 90s at sites in Peru, Argentina and Chile. They are thought to have been aged between 6 and 14 when they died. It is thought some were killed with sharp weapons, while others were buried alive, says Socha. Archaeologists beginning to excavate one of the mummies on the summit of Llullaillaco mountain J. Reinhard The researchers analysed the mummies’ hair and nail samples to determine which psychoactive plants were given to children during the capacocha ritual. Toxicological screening detected cocaine in all the hair samples, along with markers of alcohol and coca leaf chewing in half of the individuals. The team also identified harmine, a hallucinogenic compound found in the ceremonial drink ayahuasca, in one of the nail samples. Subscriber-only newsletter Sign up to Our Human Story Sign up to newsletter Socha and her colleagues suggest that the antidepressant properties of harmine could have been used to calm the children and maintain a positive mood. Each sacrifice seemed to be associated with a unique chemical signature preserved in the child’s hair and nails. This may indicate that each child was “prepared” in a different way, perhaps to direct their sacrifice towards a specific deity. “We are beginning to understand capacocha not simply as a single sacrificial event, but as a complex process involving extensive preparations, long journeys and different ritual practices,” says Socha. Journal Reference: Antiquity DOI: 10.15184/aqy.2026.10439

item.title: Diri urges Bayelsa governorship aspirants to seek God
item.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa YENAGOA — Governor Douye Diri of Bayelsa State has urged anyone aspiring to succeed him to seek God’s approval through prayer, saying the next governor must be a God-fearing person. Diri spoke on Monday during the state’s 15th Thanksgiving service at the Ecumenical Centre, Igbogene, Yenagoa, where he declared that Bayelsa had been handed over to God. He said nobody could stop anyone chosen by God to lead the state, adding that the Almighty would always have the final say in its affairs. The governor also urged residents to remain united, tolerant and peaceful, describing these as essential conditions for the state’s development. He reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to improving the lives of residents, saying it had the political will to transform Bayelsa, which he described as one of the states with the best environments for development. Diri thanked the people for their support over the past six years and urged them to sustain their cooperation with the government. “All who want to be governor, go and seek the face of God. Anyone who wants to be governor must be God-fearing. If God said yes, nobody can say no, not even me,” he said. He added: “Let us continue to worship God. Let us be tolerant and patient as we will become victorious at the end of the day. “As I keep saying, those of us who were born in Yenagoa or know Bayelsa of old can see the difference today. It is enough to give thanks. “We have one of the best environments in Nigeria, and with the political will, we are bringing development to our people.” In his sermon, the guest preacher and former Bayelsa State Chairman of the Christian Association of Nigeria, Very Rev. Joseph Opelema, urged Christians to combine their religious faith with responsible citizenship. Speaking on the theme, “Called to be Good Christians and Good Citizens,” Opelema said Christians had dual responsibilities as members of the church and citizens of society. Drawing his message from Matthew 22:15-22, where Jesus addressed the question of paying taxes, he said the biblical instruction to give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar and to God what belongs to God underscored the importance of responsible citizenship. The cleric said Christians should demonstrate sacrifice, prudence, accountability, justice, love, care and charity wherever they found themselves, particularly in public office. He lamented what he described as a gap between religious participation and the practice of Christian values, urging believers to become witnesses, the salt of the earth and the light of the world. Opelema also described Bayelsa as richly endowed with natural and human resources, favourable weather, land and rivers, which he said could make the state a tourism destination. He expressed optimism that the state could realise its potential with God-fearing leadership. item.title: North Korea slams FBI allegations over Binance hack as ‘grave’ provocation
item.description: North Korea on Tuesday slammed the FBI’s allegations that Pyongyang was behind the theft of $6 billion from cryptocurrency platform Binance, with Kim Jong Un’s powerful sister labelling it a “grave political provocation”. Kim Yo Jong, in a statement released Tuesday by the KCNA state news agency, said the FBI’s claim was “absurd rhetoric and nothing new,” given prior US allegations that North Korea was behind last year’s major hack of Bybit. “It is a grave political provocation against the DPRK that the US misleads the international public opinion as if all the cyber crimes in different parts of the world are our deeds,” Kim said, using the acronym for North Korea’s official name. The FBI said on Saturday that a North Korea-affiliated hacking group called TraderTraitor had been behind the hack. TraderTraitor is the same group blamed for a $1.5 billion theft from the Bybit platform in February last year, which had been the largest crypto theft until the Binance hack. “This is a sinister attempt to damage the international image of the DPRK and undermine its dignity and national prestige and another grave violation of the sovereignty of the DPRK,” Kim said. “It is the consistent policy stand of the DPRK government to resolutely oppose all sorts of malicious acts in cyberspace,” she added. Binance is the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes. News of the hacking attack caused the prices of most major cryptocurrencies to fall sharply on Friday. After the FBI released its statement on Saturday, US President Donald Trump cast doubt on North Korea’s involvement in the hack. “I’m not concerned. We’re learning about it. We don’t know if it’s North Korea,” Trump told reporters at his residence in Florida. Trump has made repeated overtures to nuclear-armed North Korea since returning to office, and said he was open to meeting with supreme leader Kim Jong Un this year. Those gestures have been met with silence from Pyongyang. Kim Yo Jong, in her statement, said the new allegations “confirmed Washington’s hostile attitude toward the DPRK once again.” “We have issues to reconsider in diverse aspects as regards the very unpleasant US hostile attitude,” she added. Vanguard News The post North Korea slams FBI allegations over Binance hack as ‘grave’ provocation appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Why large dogs age faster than small ones, and other October research highlights
item.description: It’s a regrettable reality that there is never enough time to cover all the interesting scientific stories we come across. So every month, we highlight a handful of the best stories that nearly slipped through the cracks. October’s list includes an epigenetic mechanism for why large dogs age faster than smaller ones; physicists who trapped a single particle of antimatter for months; and invisible tattoo inks that only show up under UV light. Why large dogs age faster In many mammalian species, larger creatures tend to have longer lifespans. Mice, for instance, live an average of just two years, while some whales can last for as long as 200 years. Dogs, however, buck this pattern; larger dogs tend to age faster and die younger than smaller ones, which makes canines an ideal model for biologists to study to learn more about aging in general. Arizona State University scientists report that these lifespan differences seem to be due to so-called "jumping genes," according to a paper published in the journal Science. The authors used data from 864 dogs collected in the Dog Aging Project to map patterns of DNA methylation (which influences how much certain genes are turned on or off) across the entire genome. It's part of the epigenome, whose markers can change over time in response to stress and other environmental factors. Genetic sequences, by contrast, are largely fixed. So DNA methylation is a good chemical indicator of aging and DNA regulation. Read full article Comments

Read Also: 2027: Obi couldn’t fix Anambra; Atiku will return to Dubai after election — Oshiomhole Wike spoke on Monday in Abuja at the commissioning of the Gwagwalada Civic Centre and an interactive session with stakeholders of the All Progressives Congress APC and the Peoples Democratic Party PDP in Gwagwalada Area Council. The minister said the coalition, which brings together political stakeholders from both parties, was formed in the interest of unity, cooperation and development in the FCT. “Some greedy and selfish politicians do not understand what we call unity. They have no capacity to hold their space, they have no capacity to even hold their families, and they have no capacity to hold their communities. So they can open their mouths and say there is no Rainbow Coalition,” he said. Wike challenged critics of the alliance to explain why political leaders who once disagreed could not come together to pursue common interests. He described the development in Gwagwalada as a departure from the politics of confrontation, insisting that the FCT needed cooperation rather than needless political hostility. Commending political leaders in the area for setting aside their differences, he said their decision showed that the collective interest of the people outweighed individual political ambition. Wike also urged residents not to repeat what he described as the mistake of the 2023 general elections, and called for credible representation at the National Assembly. The minister canvassed support for a former senator, Philip Aduda, and other candidates endorsed by the coalition, saying political representatives must be accessible and familiar with their constituents. Wike also declared support for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and urged residents to turn their endorsements into votes in 2027. “On the day of the election, it will not be a day for market or fishing. It is the day all of us have decided to come together and demonstrate our strength through our votes. Go to the polling units, districts and communities and mobilise the people to vote for Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said. item.title: EPL: Everton deepen Newcastle crisis with 1-0 win
item.description: Everton increased the pressure on under-fire Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle as Thierno Barry sealed a 1-0 win at St James’ Park on Monday. Barry netted early in the second half to lift Everton into seventh place in the Premier League and leave Newcastle languishing in 13th. Newcastle midfielder Jacob Ramsey was sent off in the final seconds for a crude foul on Harrison Armstrong. It was a fitting end to another painful defeat for Saudi-funded Newcastle, who have lost four of their past five matches in all competitions, winning just twice in their last seven. Jaissle and his players were booed off at half-time and again after the final whistle as the German coach begins to feel the heat in his first season in charge. Hired following Eddie Howe’s surprise close-season exit, former Red Bull Salzburg and Al-Ahli boss Jaissle has struggled to make an impact on Tyneside. Jaissle desperately needs a win at fellow strugglers Fulham on Saturday to ease the mounting scrutiny. Bizarrely, Newcastle have lost 22 of their last 33 Premier League matches on a Monday and many of their supporters headed for the exits well before the final whistle on a miserable rainy night. Barry’s eighth goal this season, including four in his last six matches, gave Everton their second win against Newcastle in the space of five days following their 3-1 victory in the League Cup fourth round on Thursday. Everton ended their run of two successive league defeats after losing against Arsenal and Chelsea. It was Everton’s first away league win since February 28 when they took three points on their previous visit to Newcastle. Jack Grealish was absent from the Everton squad for a second successive game after being axed for the Newcastle match last week due to a “breach of club discipline”. – Ramsey sees red – The on-loan Manchester City winger, who has been criticised for his off-field behaviour for much of his colourful career, reportedly skipped training prior to the League Cup clash. Everton said he was “not match fit” for the rematch with the Magpies, but his team coped just fine without him. Newcastle made a lively start and went close when Harvey Barnes fired just wide before Joelinton was narrowly off target from 25 yards. But chances were at a premium for both sides in a scrappy first half more notable for perspiration than inspiration. Everton’s opener four minutes after half-time was in keeping with the grimy fare that preceded it. Newcastle’s dismal marking let in Tyrique George for a shot that drew a weak save from Lukas Hornicek. Hornicek could only push it straight into the path of Barry for a simple tap-in that survived a lengthy VAR check for offside. It was a chance so easy that even the notoriously erratic Barry couldn’t fail to hit the target, although Newcastle were aggrieved by the VAR decision to let it stand. item.title: Tinubu fulfils WAFCON pledge, as Super Falcons players receive $100,000 each
item.description: The Federal Government has fulfilled President Bola Tinubu’s reward pledge to the Super Falcons following their historic 10th Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) title victory. The National Sports Commission (NSC) announced that the players, coaches and officials of the team had received their cash rewards in naira equivalent of $100,000 for each player and $50,000 for officials. The cash payments form part of the presidential reward package announced after the Super Falcons defeated their opponents to clinch their record-extending 10th WAFCON title. 𝙋𝙍𝙀𝙎𝙎 𝙍𝙀𝙇𝙀𝘼𝙎𝙀 The Federal Government, through the National Sports Commission (NSC), has fulfilled President @officialABAT Bola Ahmed Tinubu GCFR’s reward pledge to the Super Falcons @NGSuper_Falcons , with players, coaches and officials receiving their cash awards… pic.twitter.com/eGRfmA40HP — National Sports Commission (@NatSportsComm) November 2, 2026 In addition to the cash rewards, each of the players and officials had earlier received a three-bedroom flat in Abuja and the national honour of Officer of the Order of the Niger (OON). The commission celebrated the fulfilment of the presidential pledge, describing the timely disbursement of the rewards as recognition of the team’s contribution to Nigerian sports. Nigeria secured its 10th WAFCON title in July 2025 after defeating hosts Morocco 3-2 in the final, coming from two goals down to complete a remarkable comeback and maintain its dominance in African women’s football. The victory further extended the Super Falcons’ record as the most successful team in the history of the continental women’s competition. item.title: These smart glasses promise to turn your silent mouth movements into text
item.description: The next time you see a software engineer shaping silent words with their mouth, you may have to think twice before asking if they need a mental health day – they might just be wearing a pair of smart glasses that let them talk to their computer without uttering a sound. Subvocal is a Y Combinator-backed startup aiming to produce these glasses, and already has working prototypes to show off in YouTube videos, including one with YC partner Dave Lieb trying them out and being impressed enough to offer funding. The headset isn’t what the final version will look like, the company notes, which is good: The demo headset is obviously 3D printed and far from fashionable. Once the final product is available it should look a lot sleeker, based on mockups on the company’s website. It’s not clear when they’ll actually be released, though the preorder page says it’ll be sometime in Q1 2027 at an early bird price of $499. It’s not clear what the final full price will be. As for how the glasses work, the founders, Georgia Tech computer science students Aarush Yadav and Arnav Kumar, explain in a launch post on YC that the device uses low-powered radio waves projected from the glasses toward a wearer’s face. Those waves are distorted by muscle movements and the change in a person’s face shape as they speak or simply mouth words, which the duo said can be picked up and translated into written text. “We started working on this about four months ago after building the first version at a hackathon,” the pair explained in their YC post. “Since then, we’ve gone from a table full of electronics and antennas taped to our face to a semi-portable board and sleek glasses that can decode open-ended speech at 200+ WPM and a reasonably low error rate even at a small dataset scale.” This is just a proof of concept, and many key details are still missing, like the accuracy rate, battery life, whether it will paired with an app, or what-have-you. “The core thing we wanted to prove first was that the signal exists and that we can decode it,” Yadav and Kumar said. In a Hacker News post announcing the company, Yadav and Kumar explained that they started the project during the hackathon by focusing on using EMG electrodes attached to Yadav’s face. They didn’t win the hackathon, but apparently the demo was impressive enough to earn some initial funding from San Francisco VC firm Afore Capital. Shortly after that, the pair pivoted from EMG to RF sensing, as a commercial dictation product that required sticking electrodes to one’s face was unlikely to succeed. “Despite prior academic research, getting this to work was a huge engineering challenge,” Yadav said. “First we built an extremely low-noise RF sensing stack. Then we had to place antennas so their fields overlapped maximally with the articulators. Our first attempt on glasses failed completely, so we reverted to old habits and taped antennas on our face.” They eventually got to the functional prototype they have now, and pre-trai

item.title: Happy 65 Years: NASA’s Johnson Space Center Then and Now
item.description: 6 Min Read Happy 65 Years: NASA’s Johnson Space Center Then and Now View of the Manned Spacecraft Center during construction in 1963. Sixty-five years ago, a bold vision took root in Houston: a NASA center dedicated to human spaceflight. Since its founding, NASA’s Johnson Space Center has helped lead the nation’s human spaceflight program, supporting missions from Project Mercury through Artemis. Today, Johnson serves as NASA’s Center of Excellence for Human Spaceflight, and its workforce is helping to usher in a Golden Age of innovation and discovery. Johnson is home to America’s astronaut corps, the Mission Control Center, and the teams behind some of humanity’s greatest achievements in space. As NASA’s human spaceflight programs evolve, Johnson remains at the forefront of these efforts. Houston is home to NASA’s Low Earth Orbit Program, comprising International Space Station operations and commercial partnerships and destinations in low Earth orbit. For missions beyond low Earth orbit, Johnson houses the Moon Base Program⁠ and Orion Program⁠ , while NASA’s Human Health and Performance Directorate⁠ and Human Research Program ⁠ work to protect crew health and performance as missions extend farther from Earth. On May 25, 1961, the center’s story began when President John F. Kennedy gave a speech before a joint session of Congress, committing the nation to achieve the goal of landing a man on the Moon and returning him safely to Earth before the end of the decade. NASA’s Space Task Group, in charge of America’s human spaceflight program, was already working on Project Mercury to put astronauts into Earth orbit, but with the additional task of a human lunar landing, it soon outgrew its facilities at NASA’s Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia. The agency decided it needed a dedicated field center for human spaceflight and on Sept. 19, 1961, after evaluating multiple sites around the country, NASA announced that the new Manned Spacecraft Center would be built near Houston, Texas. The agency established the center on Nov. 1, 1961, and construction began in 1962. In 1973, it officially became NASA’s Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center in honor of President Johnson for his ardent support of America’s space program from its foundation. Manned Spacecraft Center to Johnson Space Center The Manned Spacecraft Center officially opened on Nov. 1, 1961, and while construction continued on the Clear Lake site, employees worked in 13 leased buildings in southeast Houston. The design phase took six months and construction of the first buildings took 18 months, with the first employees moving onto the new site in late 1963. Over the decades, the number of buildings grew, and continues to grow, to meet the demands of new spaceflight programs. View of the Manned Spacecraft Center during construction in 1963. item.title: Third person dies of bird flu since virus started jumping to livestock
item.description: A person in Washington state has died from bird flu after exposure at an infected dairy farm, state health officials reported Sunday . It marks the third human bird flu death in the US since a strain of highly pathogenic (H5) avian influenza (HPAI) made the unprecedented jump from wild, migratory birds to dairy cows, which was first reported in the US in March 2024 . The person who died was a Yakima County resident and was said to have had underlying health conditions, which could have made the person more vulnerable to the infection. On Friday, county officials reported that the person was severely ill and hospitalized . In the subsequent announcement of the person's death, officials said they would not be releasing further information about the person, including their name, gender, or age, out of respect for the family's privacy. "Our hearts go out to the individual's family and loved ones during this difficult time," Dave Atteberry, health officer for the Yakima Health District, said in a statement. "Avian influenza can cause severe illness, particularly among people who have underlying health conditions. While this is a serious and heartbreaking outcome, the risk to the general public remains low." Read full article Comments

item.title: AI could break legal systems by finding previously hidden loopholes
item.description: If AI can find the holes in programming code, it can do the same with legal code, paving the way for chaos. Felix Ringe, a visiting fellow at Stanford Law School’s liftlab and legal scholar, suggests large language models (LLMs) have become potent enough that they could break legal systems by identifying exploitable inconsistencies at scale. "Legal systems encode the foundations of social order in natural language," Ringe and collaborator Linus Folkerts argued in a blog post last week. "Similar to computer systems, the written law can contain vulnerabilities that invite exploitation." Ringe contends that while courts tend to pave over these text vulnerabilities through statutory interpretation, the ability to discover adversarially useful inconsistencies in the law in an automated way risks overwhelming the legal system's ability to bridge the gaps. To buttress his thesis, he points to recent work by other legal scholars that frames laws as vulnerable code, such as " Legal Zero-Days : A Novel Risk Vector for Advanced AI Systems" and " Hardware and Software Bugs in the Legal System " [PDF]. The analogy dates back at least to 1999, with Lawrence Lessig's Code and Other Laws of Cyberspace [PDF] and Code Is Law: On Liberty in Cyberspace . Lessig credits William J. Mitchell, in City of Bits: Space, Place, and the Infobahn (1995), with the idea that code is cyberspace's law, adding that he "drew the metaphor from others as well." Ringe has turned this on its head by proposing that law is code. The analogy between programming code and legal code works reasonably well, up to a point. Law and code both have their share of formatting pedantry and ritual. The mapping breaks down when courts get cast as a runtime environment – non-deterministic trial outcomes don't work for production applications. Discontinuities aside, Ringe's point is that AI models can surface statutory gaps at a scale that may bring the chaos currently seen in the software security ecosystem to the legal world. To demonstrate that, Ringe and Folkerts cite several potential gaps in German law that they uncovered with the help of LLMs, noting that they're only sharing legal exploits they believe could not cause serious harm. For example, an amendment to Germany's Occupational Diseases Regulation (BKV) is subject to a constitutional requirement to cite its statutory authority. But Ringe and Folkerts argue that the amendment omits a required reference. So, in theory, a journalist could request an unpublished statement submitted to Germany's occupational-diseases advisory council under freedom of information rules, challenging a confidentiality provision that the researchers argue may be invalid. Another example cited describes a transit visa rule that may be invalid because the government failed to identify the authority under which the rule was made. "We believe that with cheap legal reasoning proliferating, AI systems could jeopardize the functioning of today’s legal systems," they wrote.

item.title: [VIDEO] Umrah: No Second Term Can Be Given To Anybody Via Spiritual Claim — Atiku’s Spokesperson
item.description: Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, has criticised President Bola Tinubu’s trip to Saudi Arabia for Umrah, saying a second term in office cannot be guaranteed via a spiritual claim. The spokesperson for the ADC presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday. Shaibu said that visiting the holy land should be a personal affair and not national, accusing Tinubu’s supporters of politicising the event. ﻿ He questioned the President’s faith, saying former Kaduna State governor, Nasir El-Rufai, would not remain in custody if Tinubu had sincerity of faith. Shaibu also accused the President of speaking into a mic in Saudi Arabia while Nigerians “are dying of hunger”. He said that Tinubu administration’s claim that the economy has improved is false, as many Nigerians are facing hardship. According to him, Nigerians will remember Tinubu’s prayer in Mecca the same way they remember the high prices of food, goods and services. Asked whether Atiku would have accompanied Tinubu to Saudi Arabia if he had been invited, the aide said that the former vice president sponsored the President’s first trip to Mecca. On the chances of the ADC candidate in the 2027 presidential election across the northern states, Shaibu said Atiku is home and dry in the region. Tinubu departed Abuja for Makkah on October 29, where he performed the religious rites associated with Umrah, seeking Allah’s guidance and blessings for Nigeria and its people. Speaking shortly after completing the religious rites, which he described as a spiritual experience and an opportunity to pray for Nigeria, the President said he felt fulfilled. The All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential candidate in the 2027 general elections also said that God has granted him the wisdom to continue to lead Nigerians. “Well, I asked for wisdom and resilience to continue to serve the people. I know that has been granted. “Prior to the 2023 election, I did the same thing. I asked Allah to bless my Umrah then. He did, and I promised that I would come back to thank him, Almighty Allah. “There is no other God but him. He is the giver and the taker. “He owns the power. He said, ‘Use it well. If you don’t use it in accordance with my dictates, I can take it from you and give it to another person,’ Tinubu told journalists. “So, I have faith in that and believe extremely well that he has done me a favour to be the President of this great country.” The post [VIDEO] Umrah: No Second Term Can Be Given To Anybody Via Spiritual Claim — Atiku’s Spokesperson appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: TB 26-09 Measured Hammer-Tap Inputs
item.description: For more information, contact Joel W. Sills, Langley Research Center, joel.w.sills@nasa.gov . Download the PDF version An instrumented hammer test does not require an idealized single half-sine waveform. When the complete force and response are measured accurately, crest ripples and separated contacts remain known inputs. Force shape changes excitation, but does not inherently invalidate the record. Adequacy depends on measurement accuracy, bandwidth, signal-to-noise ratio, and coverage of the test objective. Background: What the Hammer Actually Measures Hammer tests support modal analysis [2–4] and can precede pyroshock testing [6]. Figure 1 compares a half-sine, maintained-contact rippling, and separated contacts. During a zero-force interval, the structure continues to vibrate; re-contact acts on that vibration. If an exact model and test article receive the same force and initial conditions, uniqueness gives identical responses for each bounded measured history. An approximate model can show different errors as inputs excite different frequencies, amplitudes, or nonlinear states. See [1] for the exact-model derivation. Analysis: A Half-Sine Is Broadband, but Not Flat Figure 2 shows that a finite half-sine is broadband but contains spectral zeros at f/fo = 3, 5, 7, …, with fo = 1/(2T) for pulse duration T. Its appearance alone cannot establish adequate excitation. Analysis: Spectral Content Is Determined by the Measured Force History Figure 3 normalizes each spectrum to its own DC value. Crest rippling adds content and can fill half-sine notches. Timing between separated contacts creates deterministic interference. For adequacy, inspect the unnormalized measured spectrum and response signal-to-noise ratio. Recommended Practice: Evaluate Test Adequacy Against the Intended Objective • Measure the complete applied force with adequate bandwidth, calibration, dynamic range, and time synchronization. • Verify that the response measurements have adequate bandwidth and signal-to-noise ratio and are not clipped or saturated. • Confirm that the excitation covers the frequency, amplitude, and nonlinear-response ranges required by the intended test objective. • Reject or repeat a test only for an identified measurement, excitation, or coverage deficiency. Conclusion Half-sine appearance neither establishes validity nor guarantees adequacy. Judge each hammer test by its purpose and by accurate, complete force and response measurements over the required range. References 1. A. Majed, J. Sills, E. Henkel, V. Babuska, S. Yunis, D. Hamilton, J. Akers, and T. Kinney, Validity and Predictability of Measured Hammer Tap Inputs: Linear and Nonlinear Structural Systems, September 2026. 2. D. J. Ewins, Modal Testing: Theory, Practice and Application, 2nd ed., 2000. 3. ISO 7626-5:2019, Mechanical Vibration and Shock—Experimental Determination of Mechanical Mobility—Part 5 4. K. G. McConnell and P. S. Varoto, Vibration Testing: Theory and Practice, 2nd ed., 2008. 5. A.
